subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should canonical `openai` session route state be owned for doctor cleanup by an OpenAI provider doctor contract, the Codex app-server contract, or provider-agnostic auto-fallback repair logic?
rationale: Literal `openai` is both the canonical OpenAI provider id and the provider used by Codex-backed OpenAI agent turns, so automation should not choose the permanent ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: OpenAI-Owned Doctor Contract
options.body: Add a focused OpenAI doctor owner for canonical `openai` route/auth state while keeping Codex ownership on legacy aliases and Codex runtime ids.

options.title: Codex Owns App-Server OpenAI Routes
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers define OpenAI agent turns through Codex as Codex-owned route state.

options.title: Generic Auto-Fallback Cleanup
options.body: Make doctor clear stale auto fallback overrides whenever the current configured route no longer includes the override provider, independent of plugin ownership.

recommendation.title: OpenAI-Owned Doctor Contract
recommendation.body: Add a focused OpenAI doctor owner for canonical `openai` route/auth state while keeping Codex ownership on legacy aliases and Codex runtime ids.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the clearest recent history across the Codex doctor owner, generic doctor route-state scanner, and prior merged stale-session repair PRs.
